body:
Working entry (chk-dhecc45p, Epoch 4 — Driver reliability: ledger rows and bounds): «Session folder trusted by viola
— a session viola starts in a folder the CLI never trusted opens with no trust dialog and no key typed by viola
(v2-33)».

The product write of the CLI's per-project trust record at a wrapped start: at `viola run` and `viola revive` (their
one shared start), after the version gate and before the spawn, on a verified CLI, when no record already trusts the
child's folder read the CLI's way, viola writes `projects[<key>].hasTrustDialogAccepted` (`<key>` the CLI's own key)
into the one Claude config file the started child will read, under the CLI's lock when free, by atomic replace, read
back, at most 3 attempts; a refused file form or a lost record writes nothing more and leaves the dialog to the human,
viola typing nothing. One closed word per start reaches the run log, nothing of the file anywhere. Every refusal form
gets a case proving nothing was written; the live proof is `S1` (`viola run` in a fresh untrusted folder under the
rig's private config) with its control `S2` (a plain `claude` in the same folder shape), under the founder's cap
asked at the end of P3. This chunk claims `matrix#v2-33`. Scope is the route entry and its five carries as they stand
at `2cbaa752`, nothing wider (the overseer's phase directive `phase-session-folder-directive-3.md`, item 1 — snapped
once the chunk stands).

body:
- **The founder's direction** (cry-2tyakc3h): «Ок по логике вещей надо чтоб виола так и делала если внутри нее
  создаешь сессию добавляла папку в исключения а не просто пыталась эмулировать нажатия человека»; his ruling: first
  measure whether a CLI flag or setting trusts a folder and use it; only if none, viola writes
  `projects[cwd].hasTrustDialogAccepted` (measured on 2.1.325 at chunk 2026-11-15-live-round-on-the-trimmed-product,
  its live round's entry 27: with that record no dialog rose and no key was taken). Writing the CLI's own state file
  is a boundary widening, named so, and takes its security-plan Decisions Log entry (relay
  `.andromeda/runs/2026-11-15T18-01-44-wrap/inputs/I1-e2-0.2.0-route-adaptation.md.txt`).

- **The measurement is done** (cry-igkupsjr; `p3-block.md` of the sealed run `2026-11-17T18-20-22Z-phase`, read from
  the 2.1.325 and 2.1.326 installs, no live start) — read, not re-derived (directive item 2): no flag, setting,
  environment key or managed setting only trusts a folder (`--trust-workspace` is `ultrareview`'s alone,
  `--trusted-folder` the hidden `worktree-hook`'s alone, `CLAUDE_CODE_SANDBOXED` also switches off the
  project-permission gate — named, not taken), so the ruling's second arm applies.

- **The race — R3** (cry-ewlpwxae; «Блокировка, замена, проверка», 2026-11-17, same relay): take the CLI's own lock
  when it is free, replace the file atomically, read the record back before the spawn, at most 3 attempts; a record
  still lost leaves the dialog for the human and viola types nothing; the residual — a concurrent write of another
  session lost in the window — accepted by his word and named in the row; the live cap for `S1` and `S2` is not given
  — it is asked at this take-up (directive item 5).

- **Read the CLI's way; the row is relied** (cry-3iuydqyx; `p3-block.md` of the sealed run
  `2026-11-17T22-05-41Z-phase`, read from the 2.1.325 bundle): the product write reads trust as the CLI does — the
  exact key, then the parent walk (up to the git root inside a repository, to `/` outside one; `rootOnly` dead in
  2.1.325) — so it writes no record for a folder a parent already trusts; the row it lands on, `trust-record`, read
  `pass` live on 2.1.325 (`S0B`, 2026-11-18, the rig's private config,
  `chunks/2026-11-18-trust-record-row-read-live/evidence/browser-starts.ndjson`); nothing measured on 2.1.326 or
  2.1.327 (relay `.andromeda/runs/2026-11-17T23-48-56Z-wrap/inputs/I1-split-reread-route-adaptation.md.txt`).

- [inferred] **The writer already stands**: `crates/viola-agent-claude/src/trust.rs` (the record's shape, the key
  rule) and `src/trust_record.rs` (the file write: lock, atomic replace keeping the file's mode, the refusals, 14
  closed code words), built for verify's Run F by `2026-11-17-trust-record-ledger-row`; the product write reuses it
  rather than adding a second writer. To close at P3: what it already refuses, whether it has a read-back and a retry,
  whether it reads trust with the parent walk, and what it writes for an absent entry.

- [inferred] **The fake agent already reads the record** (its trust decision from the Claude config file, not argv
  alone — the cancelled take-up's correction 3, built by `2026-11-17-trust-record-ledger-row`), so an e2e case of the
  write can FAIL when viola's write is gone. To close at P3 against `src/bin/viola-fake-agent` (or wherever the fake
  lives) and its `--trust-config` / trust reading; a change to its screens or its trust reading puts `cli_verify` in the
  gate block (directive item 8).

- [inferred] **«On a verified CLI» after the 23rd row** (directive item 4): a stamp taken at 22 rows reads unverified to
  a binary built from this tree, so `run` on a home whose stamp predates the row is transport-only and writes NO trust
  record — the dialog stays the human's — until that home's next live verify. Nothing is re-pinned by this chunk; the
  pinned product the overseer drives with is untouched. To close at P3 against `run`'s version gate
  (`read_stamps_strict`, `cli_verified`).

Each of these gets a case proving NOTHING was written (the file's bytes unchanged, no temp sibling left, no lock left):
the file absent (no create), unreadable, a link, not the JSON expected (not an object, `projects` not an object, the
entry not an object), oversize (past `MAX_FRAME`), a lost race (the record not read back after the 3rd attempt), and
the skips that are no refusal: an unverified CLI, a folder the exact key or a parent already trusts, the home folder.

   (c) the predicate of each live entry, one its reading can FAIL: `S1` RED when the first screen reads `trust` or
   the sentinel entry differs by a byte or the written record is not exactly the one key; `S2` RED when the first
   screen does NOT read `trust`; both RED on a teardown word missing;

   that the founder's real `~/.claude.json` is read only by the mark witness.

   Plan every other step on the fake agent meanwhile.

10. A leaf comparer's re-spawn on a `leaves --apply` receipt refusal: if the guard blocks the `--rows` form, STOP

11. Call NO scheduled-wake or timer tool, with any argument. End every process you start.

The founder's own answers, given in the overseer's dialog and read at 2026-11-18T11:39:23Z (his options, verbatim labels), to your
size-first block; then the technical answers. Take P4 on these and go on to the P5 card.

## The founder's answers

1. **The live cap for THIS chunk — «S1: 1 + 1 запасной, S2: 1».** `S1`: ONE rig start that carries its own live
   `viola verify` (step 1, in a separate trusted git folder; all 23 rows must pass or step 2 does not start) and
   then `viola run` in the fresh untrusted folder — 8 `claude` processes — plus ONE spare. `S2`: ONE start of a
   plain `claude` in the same folder shape, no spare. All on the 2.1.325 install by path, under the rig's private
   config. So: S1 carrying a live verify of its own is ACCEPTED. The spare is spent only on a cause a start
   ITSELF showed (a kept frame or screen, a closed word), after its mend lands through a plan revision — never on
   an inference. Each start is ledgered with the clock's time before it is made; a start refused for the token
   window is uncounted — stop and say so, no timer. A further start is his.
2. **Keys: none.** The rig types nothing into any dialog or box in either start (verify pastes only its own
   ratified literals into its own run). **The stop, named for each start:** in `S1`, Ctrl-C into the rig's own pty
   ONLY when the input box stands, the no-key group kill when a dialog stands; `S2` always the no-key group kill.
   The summary prints `stop:` beside `keys:`.
3. **No split.**
4. **F-T1 — «Ставит флаг, остальное не трогает».** Where an entry already stands at the key without a true flag
   (absent or `false`), viola sets ONLY `hasTrustDialogAccepted` in it and keeps every other key of that entry
   byte for byte. He was told its price in the dialog: a human's earlier «no» for that folder cannot be told from a
   closed dialog, and a session started through viola in it overrides either. The plan words this in the row it
   amends and gives it a case (an entry with other keys and the flag `false` → the flag `true`, every other key
   equal) and a case each for the flag absent and for the flag already `true` (nothing written).

## Technical answers (the overseer's)

5. **F-T2 — the run log's word:** a new `trust-record{detail}` event, once per start, with its obs Decisions Log
   entry and schema update as Expected amendments; its detail a closed word (`written` · `already-trusted` ·
   `parent-trusted` · `unverified-cli` · the writer's refusal words), nothing of the file.
6. **The unmeasured case you named** — the real CLI adding keys to the new entry before its first screen — is
   handled in the predicate's wording, not by loosening it: `S1` reads the entry viola wrote at the moment the
   WRITER read it back (the writer's own read-back, before the spawn) for «exactly the one key», and the entry at
   the first settled screen only for `hasTrustDialogAccepted: true` still standing. Say so in the plan.
7. Every live entry keeps a predicate its reading can fail, as your block's (c) lists; step 1 of `S1` reads the
   21-row floor and `trust-record: pass` before step 2 may start; the browser-tools key is seeded for both arms.
8. **The seam after P5.** When the plan is approved the phase ENDS and nothing else starts: the founder is closing
   the overseer sessions, and implement — with its live starts — is the next window's first act.

_Generated by /andromeda-phase P4. Read by /andromeda-implement. Manual edits between runs are fine; do not
edit during an /implement run._
- **Marker:** 2026-11-18-session-folder-trusted-by-viola · **Version:** viola-0.2.0 · **Generated:** 2026-11-18T11:44:43Z

A session viola starts — `viola run`, or a `viola revive` whose preflight passed (one shared `start`,
`src/cmd/run.rs:260`, called by `src/cmd/revive.rs:154`) — in a folder the CLI never trusted opens at its input box with
no trust dialog and no key typed by viola. Directly after the version gate and before the endpoint bind, on a verified
CLI only, viola reads the one Claude config file the child will read the CLI's way (the exact key, then the parent
walk), and when nothing trusts the folder it writes `projects[<the CLI's key>].hasTrustDialogAccepted = true` there:
ONLY that field, for one folder, under the CLI's lock when free, by atomic replace keeping the file's mode, read back
exact, at most 3 attempts. A file absent, unreadable, a link, not regular, foreign, oversize or not the JSON expected
writes nothing and leaves the dialog to the human; so does a lost record. Each start writes ONE closed word to the run
log, nothing of the file anywhere. This is the founder's ratified bound (R2 «Файл ребёнка, ключ как у CLI», R3
«Блокировка, замена, проверка», carries cry-hstbfhw4 / cry-ewlpwxae) and his answer F-T1 «Ставит флаг, остальное не
трогает» (inputs#I2 item 4), read as the security plan's boundary-widening class
(`(security-plan · data-protection/decision/no-writes-under-claude-home)` is amended at the wrap).

The writer already stands (`src/trust_record.rs`, built for verify's Run F): its checks, lock, replace, read-back and
3 attempts are reused, no second writer (`(security-plan · authentication-authorization/decision/one-replace-helper)`,
`(architecture · established-decisions/decision/tempfile-snapshot-writer)`). New here: the CLI's trust read with the
parent walk, the flag-only set into an existing entry (F-T1), the exact read-back (inputs#I2 item 6), the home-folder
skip, the start's call and its one `trust-record` log line (inputs#I2 item 5), the fake agent's parent walk, the e2e
proof on the fake agent, and the live proof `S1` with its control `S2` on 2.1.325 under the founder's cap (inputs#I2
items 1–2). On a home stamped before the 23rd row the CLI reads unverified and the start writes nothing
(`(architecture · standard-contracts/decision/version-verified-all-relied-rows)`; `src/run/version_gate.rs:286-287`).
Claims `matrix#v2-33`.

1. **The CLI's trust read — `crates/viola-agent-claude/src/trust.rs`** (pure, no I/O,
   `(architecture · crate-dependency-direction/decision/agent-claude-pure)`). Add a read of a config document's bytes
   against the canonical cwd and its git root (`Option`) that answers one of: trusted at the key viola would write
   (`record_key`), trusted at another folder on the walk, or not trusted. The walk is the CLI 2.1.325 bundle's `SS`
   (sealed block 2 (ii), carry cry-3iuydqyx): start at the cwd; a folder counts when
   `projects[<folder>].hasTrustDialogAccepted == true` (a boolean `true`, nothing else); stop after the git root inside
   a repository, after `/` outside one; a folder above the git root never counts. Keys are the folders' lossless
   `to_string_lossy` spellings, as `record_key` already writes them.

2. **The flag-only set (F-T1) — the same file.** Add the change the start writes: no entry at the key → insert
   `{"hasTrustDialogAccepted": true}`; an entry that is an object whose flag is absent or `false` → set ONLY that field
   to `true`, every other key of the entry kept in place and value (`preserve_order` is on,
   `(architecture · stack-and-technologies/decision/preserve-key-order)`); an entry that is not an object, or whose
   flag is any other value, → `config-malformed`, nothing changed. The document's other keys and entries are kept as
   `with_record` keeps them. `with_record` stays as it is for verify's Run F (its `key-present` unchanged there).
   Add the exact read-back predicate: the entry at the key equals the entry this change produced, value for value.

3. **The start's closed words — the same file.** A closed enum of the start's outcomes, each a code word
   (`(security-plan · input-validation/decision/trust-record-closed-words)`; obs standing S3): `written` ·
   `already-trusted` (the walk found the record at the key viola would write) · `parent-trusted` (found at another
   folder on the walk) · `unverified-cli` · `home-folder` (the key viola would write is the user home) · and the
   writer's refusal words `config-absent` · `config-unreadable` · `config-link` · `config-not-regular` ·
   `config-foreign` · `config-oversize` · `config-malformed` · `config-dir-unusable` · `home-unknown` · `lock-held` ·
   `lost` — 16 words, listed literally in its unit test, each through `viola_core::is_code_word`. `home-folder` is
   this plan's addition to the relay's list (inputs#I2 item 5 names «the writer's refusal words»; the home-folder skip is
   R2's «nothing written for the home folder», which no writer word names).

4. **The product write — `src/trust_record.rs`.** Add one `pub(crate)` entry for the start that takes the config file,
   the canonical cwd, the git root and the user home, and returns one word of step 3. It runs the existing attempt
   loop (`change`, at most `ATTEMPTS` = 3, `LOCK_PAUSE` 100 ms) with a third `Change` kind: `checked` → `Lock::take` →
   `read` (unchanged: `O_NOFOLLOW`, `take(MAX_FRAME + 1)`) → step 1's walk (trusted → `already-trusted` /
   `parent-trusted`, nothing written, the lock dropped) → step 2's change → `replace_private(file, …, mode & 0o7777)`
   → lock dropped → the read-back with step 2's exact predicate (a mismatch, a racing writer's added key included, is
   `Again(Lost)`). The home-folder rule runs before any open: the key equals the canonical user home → `home-folder`.
   `write_record` / `remove_record` and verify's behaviour are unchanged. The writer still writes no log line
   (`src/trust_record.rs:6-7`).

5. **The config-file choice shared — `src/cmd/verify.rs` → `src/trust_record.rs`.** Move `trust_config_file(strip)`
   (`src/cmd/verify.rs:322-330`) into `src/trust_record.rs` unchanged and re-point verify's one call (`measure`,
   `src/cmd/verify.rs:234`). The `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` value is still read only when the strip keeps the name
   (`(security-plan · secret-management/decision/credential-strip-by-name-only)`, amended at the wrap to name the
   start).

6. **The call in the start — `src/cmd/run.rs`.** Directly after `version_gate` (`src/cmd/run.rs:289`) and before
   `bind_endpoint`: when `gate.cli_verified` is false the word is `unverified-cli` and nothing is read; else
   `trust_config_file(&strip)` (its error word stands), the canonical `launch.spawn_dir` (revive's recorded cwd;
   a canonicalisation failure reads `config-unreadable` and writes nothing — no new word), its `git_root`, the user
   home (`std::env::home_dir()`, canonicalised), then step 4's entry. Write ONE `obs_event!(INFO, ObsEvent::TrustRecord,
   detail = <word>)` inside the `run.start` span, no path, key, value, cwd or file name in it; no new span (the chain
   `(obs-plan · span-trace-coverage/contract/run-start-spans/span-chain)` is unchanged). The word never refuses the
   start, prints nothing and adds no exit code or `revive --json` code
   (`(design-system · surface-cli/decision/silent-catch-sites)`, design history 2–3).

7. **The obs event — `crates/viola-core/src/obs.rs`, `schemas/diag-line.v1.json`.** Add the `ObsEvent` variant
   `TrustRecord` (kebab `trust-record`) and its `detail` enum of step 3's 16 words to the default-deny schema
   (`(obs-plan · 8-pii-scrubbing-compliance/decision/default-deny-log-fields)`; obs standing S3, S5). The schema's event
   enum equals the variants (`(obs-plan · bootstrap-phases-derive-for-route-setup-project/decision/diag-schema-matches-event-enum)`).

8. **The fake agent's parent walk — `src/bin/viola-fake-agent.rs`, `src/bin/viola-fake-agent/test_cases_opts.rs`.**
   `record_trusts` reads step 1's walk by its own code (not the product's, `(test-plan · 11-test-anti-patterns-never-do-these/decision/literal-test-oracles)`):
   from the canonical cwd up, the nearest `.git` ancestor the stop (else `/`), a boolean `true` flag counting. Its unit
   cases add: a parent record trusts a subfolder outside a repository; a record above the git root does not; a `false`
   flag does not. This changes the fake's trust reading, so `cli_verify` is in the gate block
   (verification-harness.md 2026-11-17).

9. **Test support — `tests/support/home.rs`.** Add `Wrapper::boot_untrusted_as_user(stamped, name, user_home, extra)`
   beside `boot_untrusted` and `boot_as_user` (`tests/support/home.rs:692`, `:715`): the fake agent's cwd untrusted
   (no `--trusted-root`), the wrapper given `user_home` as `HOME`, the tied builder kept
   (`(test-plan · integration-test-strategy/decision/wrapper-drop-guard)`). The user home is made by `private_dir` and
   its `.claude.json` seeded owner-only by the case (a CLI file, no viola state file; tests history 32).

10. **The integration cases — `tests/run_cli.rs`, `tests/cli_revive.rs`, `tests/tui_passthrough.rs`** (keeps tests
    S1–S3, S6, S7; obs S1, S2; security S1). Every case boots under its own home and its own user home, the fake agent
    given `--screens --trust-config <user home>/.claude.json`, the config seeded with one sentinel entry of another
    folder (`{"hasTrustDialogAccepted": true, "allowedTools": []}`); waits key on records under `WITHIN`:
    - `run_in_an_untrusted_folder_writes_the_record_and_types_no_key` (stamped): the run log holds exactly one
      `trust-record` line, `detail` `written`; the events from the start's own offset read `wheel{cause:start}` then
      `session-start` with no `wheel{human-input}`; the fake's receipt holds no `key` line before its SessionStart hook;
      `projects[<canonical cwd>]` is exactly `{"hasTrustDialogAccepted": true}`; the sentinel's serialised bytes equal;
      no `.claude.json.lock` and no temp sibling left.
    - `run_with_the_entry_flag_false_sets_only_the_flag`: the seeded entry `{"hasTrustDialogAccepted": false,
      "allowedTools": ["x"], "k": 1}` → the flag `true`, every other key equal, `written`.
    - `run_with_the_flag_already_true_writes_nothing`: `already-trusted`, the file's bytes equal.
    - `run_under_a_trusted_parent_writes_nothing`: the parent's record trusts the cwd, `parent-trusted`, bytes equal,
      the session starts (the fake's walk).
    - `run_on_an_unverified_home_writes_nothing` (`StampedHome::unstamped`): `unverified-cli`, bytes equal, no
      SessionStart (the dialog stands).
    - `run_in_the_user_home_writes_nothing`: the cwd is the test user home, `home-folder`, bytes equal.
    - `run_with_the_config_dir_kept_writes_that_file`: `claude_env_keep: ["CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR"]` in the home's
      `config.json`, `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` set on the wrapper alone, the fake told `<dir>/.claude.json`: the record
      lands there, the `HOME` file's bytes equal.
    - `run_trust_refusals_write_nothing` (rstest table, one case each: `absent`, `link`, `not_regular`, `malformed`,
      `oversize`, `lock_held`): its word on the run log, the path's bytes (or absence) and the lock dir as found, no
      SessionStart (the dialog stands); the `written` case above is the control that the path reaches the write (tests
      history 20).
    - `revive_writes_the_record_for_its_recorded_cwd` (`tests/cli_revive.rs`, `start.rs`'s shared setups): the revived
      start's run-log word `written` for the recorded cwd's key, not the reviving process's own directory.
    - `passthrough_of_a_trust_writing_start_adds_no_viola_bytes` (`tests/tui_passthrough.rs`, a11y history 2): the outer
      PTY stream holds no viola-originated byte compared with an unwrapped fake run.

11. **Unit cases** — `crates/viola-agent-claude/src/trust.rs`: `trust_walk_reads_the_exact_key_then_each_parent`
    (table: exact key, parent outside a repository up to `/`, parent inside up to the root, above the root, flag
    `false`, flag `"true"`), `flag_only_set_keeps_every_other_key` (absent entry, flag absent, flag false, non-object

    `trust_start_flag_false_sets_only_the_flag`, `trust_start_already_trusted_writes_nothing`,
    `trust_start_parent_trusted_writes_nothing`, `trust_start_home_folder_opens_nothing`,
    `trust_start_refusals_write_nothing` (absent, unreadable mode 000, link, dir, foreign by injected euid, oversize,
    malformed — bytes, lock and siblings as found), `trust_start_lost_after_three_read_backs` (the `read_back` hook),
    `trust_start_read_back_with_an_added_key_is_lost`; `src/cmd/run.rs`: the start's unverified arm reads no file.

12. **The rig's two arms — `crates/viola-e2e/src/rig/mod.rs`, `rig/isolate.rs`, `src/bin/viola-live-rig.rs`.**
    - Arm `TS` (labels `S1`, `S1-2`): one scratch, its `vhome` keeping `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`. Step 1: `vcwd/`
      git-initialised (`make_git_root`) and seeded trusted at its root's key, `viola --home <vhome> verify -- <program>`

      item 6), `sentinel:` (`equal` · `differs`). Keys: none. Stop: `box` read → the standing Ctrl-C into its own pty;
      a dialog read → the no-key group kill (`stop_no_key`); `keys:` and `stop:` printed side by side.
    - Arm `TC` (label `S2`): a fresh `cwd/` of the same shape, the same seed and sentinel, plain `<program> --model
      haiku`, no viola; prints `first-screen:`; stop always the no-key group kill.
    - Both arms seed `hasCompletedOnboarding`, the used-config markers and `claudeInChromeDefaultEnabled: false`

13. **The rehearsals — `crates/viola-e2e/tests/rig_rehearsal.rs`.** Over the fake agent:
    `rig_rehearsal_ts_verifies_then_runs_and_reads_the_written_record` (step 1's verify over the fake as the `V`

14. **The live starts** (the last thing before the operator pass; the fake-agent work green and in the tree first):
    `S1` then `S2` on 2.1.325 by path, each ledgered with `date -u` before it is made, under the founder's cap (S1 1 +

The block runs the formatter and linter, the agent crate's unit suite, the root unit layer, the changed integration

(the stamping helpers, the harness boot and the rig rehearsals reach every stamped binary), the schema and
bounded-reader contracts, the release check (the fake agent changed), the live round (S1, S2) and the operator pass.
Every root test that waits keeps the shared 12 s `WITHIN` under the 20 s lint; the rig rehearsal of `TS` drives a
verify and sits where the `V` rehearsal sits, its kill the one that binary already has. The harness boot is not a
touchpoint and no boot-path file changes beyond the start (`src/cmd/run.rs` is exercised by every booted case), so the
operator pass boots one session `trust-smoke` as the last chunk did and reads it. No mutation run (directive item 7).

The remove-the-guard controls are implement's one-shot `gate.py control` runs, not entries (validation.md check 4 (6)),
each fired with `--timeout 900` (sized to the integration entry's build plus its named cases, each case bounded by
`WITHIN`), each control's entry named; «holds» means each named case ran and FAILED with no TIMEOUT line:

- `trust-nocall` — `src/cmd/run.rs`: the start's trust call removed (no file read, no line); entry: the named
  integration entry; case `run_in_an_untrusted_folder_writes_the_record_and_types_no_key`. With the guard gone the
  subject starts its child in the untrusted folder, the fake draws the trust form and fires no SessionStart; the case's
  wait for it ends at `WITHIN` — unmeasured until this control runs.

- `trust-gate` — `src/cmd/run.rs`: the `cli_verified` arm removed (the write made on an unverified CLI); entry: the
  named integration entry; case `run_on_an_unverified_home_writes_nothing`. With the guard gone the record is written on
  an unverified home — unmeasured until this control runs.

- `trust-walk` — `crates/viola-agent-claude/src/trust.rs`: the walk cut to the exact key; entry: `cargo nextest run -p
  viola-agent-claude`; case `trust_walk_reads_the_exact_key_then_each_parent`. With the guard gone a subfolder of a
  trusted parent is written a needless record — unmeasured until this control runs.

- `trust-exact` — `src/trust_record.rs`: the read-back cut to the flag alone; entry: `bash scripts/agent-run.sh run
  --unit`; case `trust_start_read_back_with_an_added_key_is_lost`. With the guard gone a raced entry reads `written` —
  unmeasured.

body:
- (product, matrix#v2-33) A session viola starts in a folder the CLI has never trusted, on a CLI version whose stamp
  holds every relied row `pass`, opens at its input box with no trust dialog shown and no key typed by viola, viola
  having written exactly `projects[<the CLI's key>].hasTrustDialogAccepted = true` into the config file the child reads
  and every other folder's entry unchanged: on the fake agent `run_in_an_untrusted_folder_writes_the_record_and_types_no_key`
  and `revive_writes_the_record_for_its_recorded_cwd` (the integration entry), live on 2.1.325 `S1` reading
  `first-screen: box`, `run-trust: written`, `entry-flag: true`, `sentinel: equal` against `S2` reading
  `first-screen: trust` (the two live entries).

- (security) Each refusal form writes nothing and leaves the dialog to the human: `run_trust_refusals_write_nothing`
  (absent, link, not regular, malformed, oversize, lock held) and `trust_start_refusals_write_nothing` /
  `trust_start_lost_after_three_read_backs` (unreadable, foreign, lost) — bytes, lock and siblings as found
  (`(security-plan · data-protection/decision/trust-record-writer-guarded)`; directive item 7).

- (security) No record on an unverified CLI, for a folder the exact key or a parent already trusts, or for the home
  folder: `run_on_an_unverified_home_writes_nothing`, `run_with_the_flag_already_true_writes_nothing`,
  `run_under_a_trusted_parent_writes_nothing`, `run_in_the_user_home_writes_nothing`.

- (security, F-T1) An entry standing without a true flag gets only the flag:
  `run_with_the_entry_flag_false_sets_only_the_flag` and `flag_only_set_keeps_every_other_key` (inputs#I2 item 4).
- (security) The file is the one the child reads: `run_with_the_config_dir_kept_writes_that_file`.
- (a11y) A trust-writing start puts no viola byte on the terminal: `passthrough_of_a_trust_writing_start_adds_no_viola_bytes`.

- (tests) The changed binaries, the whole integration and E2E layers and both unit entries return green; the six
  controls read «holds».

- Spec anchors: `(security-plan · data-protection/decision/no-writes-under-claude-home)`,
  `(security-plan · data-protection/decision/trust-record-writer-guarded)`,
  `(security-plan · input-validation/decision/trust-record-closed-words)`,
  `(security-plan · secret-management/decision/r8-claude-env-strip)`,
  `(architecture · established-decisions/decision/verify-own-trust-record)`,
  `(architecture · established-decisions/decision/run-start-order)`,
  `(architecture · standard-contracts/decision/version-verified-all-relied-rows)`,
  `(obs-plan · 4-span-trace-coverage/decision/trust-record-write-uninstrumented)`,
  `(obs-plan · 8-pii-scrubbing-compliance/decision/default-deny-log-fields)`,
  `(test-plan · 7-test-data-fixtures/contract/fake-agent-cli/trust-config)`,
  `(test-plan · 6-e2e-test-strategy/decision/standing-live-rig)`,
  `(a11y-plan · cognitive-accessibility/decision/time-bounds-fall-on-the-driver)`.
- External inputs: inputs#I1 (the directive), inputs#I2 (the founder's answers and the overseer's technical answers).

- Research files inspected: `src/trust_record.rs`, `crates/viola-agent-claude/src/trust.rs`, `src/cmd/verify.rs`,
  `src/cmd/run.rs`, `src/cmd/revive.rs`, `src/run/version_gate.rs`, `src/bin/viola-fake-agent.rs`,
  `crates/viola-e2e/src/rig/mod.rs`, `crates/viola-e2e/src/rig/isolate.rs`, `tests/support/home.rs`.

- A second writer for the start — rejected: the guarded writer is the one the rows name, its mode-keeping replace the
  one exception to `(security-plan · authentication-authorization/decision/explicit-mode-before-write)`.

- A start refusal, exit code, hint or `revive --json` code for any trust word — rejected: the write never refuses the
  start (design history 2–3, layouts history 5).
- Typing a key into the trust dialog, by viola or by the rig — rejected (`(architecture · established-decisions/decision/no-typing-into-trust-dialogs)`; keys none, inputs#I2 item 2).
- Creating an absent config, or writing into the founder's real `~/.claude.json` in a live start — rejected (R2; S1 writes the rig's private config through the kept `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`).
- A span for the write — rejected: the start chain stays as it is, one line only (obs history 10, 14).
- Writing the stamps for S1's home from anything but `viola verify` — rejected (`(architecture · standard-contracts/contract/ledger-stamps/writer)`); S1 carries its own verify (inputs#I2 item 1).
- Re-reading the stamps for the write's gate — rejected: it reads `gate.cli_verified` only (security history 22).

- The `S1` predicate (inputs#I2 item 6): «exactly the one key» is read at the moment the WRITER read it back, before the
  spawn — `run-trust: written` certifies it, since step 4's read-back is the exact predicate of step 2; the entry at the
  first settled screen is read only for `hasTrustDialogAccepted: true` still standing (`entry-flag: true`). Whether the
  real CLI adds keys to the entry before its first screen stays unmeasured and cannot redden S1.

- F-T1's price, as the founder was told (inputs#I2 item 4): a human's earlier «no» for a folder cannot be told from a
  closed dialog, and a session started through viola in it overrides either. The wrap words this in the row it amends.
- The record persists: unlike verify's, the start's record is never removed (security history 2, 6).
- The race residual (R3): a concurrent write of another session lost in the window, accepted by the founder's word.

- The `gpt()` residual (sealed block 2 (ii)): the CLI still shows the dialog for a folder trusted only by an ancestor
  holding project or local settings; viola reads «parent-trusted», writes nothing, and the dialog is the human's.
- The time bound of the start's lock pauses (at most 2 × 100 ms) falls on viola's own start, never on a human key.

- The cap: S1 1 + 1 spare (S1-2), S2 1, no spare; keys none; stop as named (inputs#I2 items 1–2). Each start ledgered
  with `date -u` before it is made; a token-window refusal uncounted, no timer.
- The phase ends at the P5 word; implement, with its live starts, is the next window's first act (inputs#I2 item 8).

- Expected amendments (wrap) — each a boundary widening of the class `rul-r74hshif` / `rul-bznresq5`, answered by the
  founder himself (R2 and R3, relay `.andromeda/runs/2026-11-17T19-03-40Z-wrap/inputs/I1-split-trust-route-adaptation.md.txt`;
  F-T1 and the S1 shape with its sentinel seed, inputs#I2, relayed verbatim by the overseer) unless marked otherwise:
  - security-plan §Data Protection — `(security-plan · data-protection/decision/no-writes-under-claude-home)`,
    `(security-plan · data-protection/decision/viola-writes-nothing-in-claude-dir)`,
    `(security-plan · threat-model-summary/decision/nothing-written-under-claude-home)`: the start's flag-only write
    beside verify's own, the record persisting, F-T1's price named; `(security-plan · data-protection/decision/trust-record-writer-guarded)`:
    the start's flag-only set into an existing entry and its exact read-back; plus the security Decisions Log entry for
    the widening.
  - security-plan §Input Validation — `(security-plan · input-validation/decision/trust-record-closed-words)`: the
    start's 16 words; `(security-plan · input-validation/decision/revive-cwd-spawn-only)` and
    `(security-plan · input-validation/decision/revive-recorded-cwd-spawn-dir)`: the recorded cwd also keys the start's

# Implement directive — «Session folder trusted by viola» (chunk 2026-11-18-session-folder-trusted-by-viola)

The plan is approved (rev 2). This window is fresh: read the chunk's run dir and documents from disk first.

## The live cap for THIS chunk (the founder's own answers, read 2026-11-18T11:39:23Z; unchanged, nothing widens it)

- **`S1`: ONE rig start + ONE spare.** The start carries its own live `viola verify` (step 1, in a separate
  trusted git folder; all 23 rows pass or step 2 does not start), then `viola run` in the fresh untrusted folder —
  8 `claude` processes. **`S2`: ONE start of a plain `claude`, no spare.** All on the 2.1.325 install by path,
  under the rig's private config, the scratch folders outside every repository.
- **The spare is spent only on a cause a start ITSELF showed** (a kept frame or screen, a closed word), after its
  mend lands through a plan revision — never on an inference. A further start is the founder's.
- **Keys: none.** The rig types nothing into any dialog or box. **The stop:** in `S1`, Ctrl-C into the rig's own
  pty ONLY when the input box stands, the no-key group kill when a dialog stands; `S2` always the no-key group
  kill. The summary prints `stop:` beside `keys:`.
- Each start is ledgered with the clock's time (`date -u`) BEFORE it is made. A start refused for the token
  window is uncounted — stop and say so; set no timer and no scheduled wake of your own.
- An entry already at the key without a true flag gets `hasTrustDialogAccepted` ALONE, every other key byte for
  byte.

## Stops

- **A RED live entry stops implement BEFORE the operator pass**: report the entry, what the start itself showed,
  and wait. A red that moves a plan entry is revised through the phase's door, not patched here.
- A guard block of a leaf re-spawn's old `--rows` form: stop and say so; do not route around it.
- The rig keeps its screens locally and lands closed words only; nothing of the operator's status line or config
  enters a commit.

## On green

Write the chunk report (P4), then run the operator pass in this same window with the `ci.py conclusion` read
(leg=operator) as usual, and land `evidence/operator-pass.md`. Then stop: the wrap is a fresh window's.

Measured in the artifacts: `evidence/live-starts.ndjson` holds one start line (`S1`, 2026-11-18T13:13:26Z) and its
summary; `rig/ledger.rs` `admit` counts every base label in the ledger FILE against `--cap`; plan entries 12 and 14
both name that file with `--cap 1`. So `S2` was refused before its ledger line: no `claude` ran, the start is
uncounted and unspent. `S1` is green and is NOT run again; its spare stays unspent and is not needed.

1. **The mend — entry 14 alone: `--cap 2 --spare 0`, the SAME ledger.** One ledger a chunk stays the evidence both
   entries name; two base starts in it (`S1`, `S2`) is exactly the cap that stands (S1 one + one spare, S2 one, no
   spare). No ledger of its own for `S2`, no change to the rig's `admit`, no change to entry 12. Say in the plan's
   cap line that `--cap` is the count of base starts in the ledger file, so the second arm's number is the total.
2. **The cap is unchanged.** `S2`: ONE start of a plain `claude`, no spare, keys none, the stop the no-key group
   kill; ledgered with `date -u` before it is made; a start refused for the token window is uncounted — stop and
   say so, no timer.
3. **The files beyond the plan.** The ten files that give every test start and the harness's wrappers a test-owned
   user home enter the plan's file list at this revision's list sync, with the one line that says why (a start
   under the real `HOME` would write a trust record into the operator's real config). Nothing else moves.
4. **Research at this revision:** none beyond the list sync and `rig/ledger.rs` `admit`. The card: the changed
   lines only.
5. **After the approval** the phase ENDS. Implement then resumes at entry 14 alone (`--live-legs --entry 14`), reads
   `S2` against `S1`, and on green writes the report and runs the operator pass with the `ci.py conclusion` read as
   usual. A RED `S2` stops implement before the operator pass.

body:
# Implement directive — «Session folder trusted by viola» (chunk 2026-11-18-session-folder-trusted-by-viola)

The plan is approved (rev 2). This window is fresh: read the chunk's run dir and documents from disk first.

## The live cap for THIS chunk (the founder's own answers, read 2026-11-18T11:39:23Z; unchanged, nothing widens it)

- **`S1`: ONE rig start + ONE spare.** The start carries its own live `viola verify` (step 1, in a separate
  trusted git folder; all 23 rows pass or step 2 does not start), then `viola run` in the fresh untrusted folder —
  8 `claude` processes. **`S2`: ONE start of a plain `claude`, no spare.** All on the 2.1.325 install by path,
  under the rig's private config, the scratch folders outside every repository.
- **The spare is spent only on a cause a start ITSELF showed** (a kept frame or screen, a closed word), after its
  mend lands through a plan revision — never on an inference. A further start is the founder's.
- **Keys: none.** The rig types nothing into any dialog or box. **The stop:** in `S1`, Ctrl-C into the rig's own
  pty ONLY when the input box stands, the no-key group kill when a dialog stands; `S2` always the no-key group
  kill. The summary prints `stop:` beside `keys:`.
- Each start is ledgered with the clock's time (`date -u`) BEFORE it is made. A start refused for the token
  window is uncounted — stop and say so; set no timer and no scheduled wake of your own.
- An entry already at the key without a true flag gets `hasTrustDialogAccepted` ALONE, every other key byte for
  byte.

## Stops

- **A RED live entry stops implement BEFORE the operator pass**: report the entry, what the start itself showed,
  and wait. A red that moves a plan entry is revised through the phase's door, not patched here.
- A guard block of a leaf re-spawn's old `--rows` form: stop and say so; do not route around it.
- The rig keeps its screens locally and lands closed words only; nothing of the operator's status line or config
  enters a commit.

## On green

Write the chunk report (P4), then run the operator pass in this same window with the `ci.py conclusion` read
(leg=operator) as usual, and land `evidence/operator-pass.md`. Then stop: the wrap is a fresh window's.

ledger and the outcome files, not from memory. The operator is AWAY: no question waits for him. A fork comes to the
overseer as a dialog; an answer card whose every row lies inside the founder's own recorded answers is confirmed by
the overseer; a boundary widening OUTSIDE those answers takes its most conservative option and is written to
`founder-forks.md`.

- Every time bound viola holds (wait timeout and cap, dialog hold, send readiness gate, confirmation windows, agents read, the start's Claude config lock wait) falls on the driver, viola's child or viola's own start; no key is blocked, refused or delayed by it. The one `claude agents --json` read `viola list` and `viola revive` each make (chunk 2026-10-16-unwrapped-sessions-on-the-board) is killed at 5 s, a bound on viola's own child only: a failed, oversize, malformed or timed-out read fails open, and no key is blocked, refused or delayed by it. `viola wait` returns `{timed_out:true}` only for a timeout the caller passes in. The MCP `wait` tool (chunk 2026-10-17-mcp-server-for-drivers) clamps its `timeout_ms` to `WAIT_CAP` 50 000 ms, also its default when the caller passes none (`viola_mcp::wait_timeout`), so an MCP `wait` with no timeout is answered `timed-out` after 50 s: a bound on the driver only (the hidden, plugin-run `viola mcp` serves a driving Claude session, never a person), no key is blocked, refused or delayed by it, and the wheel is untouched. A raised dialog takes a `viola answer` only within the dialog hold (`config.json`'s `dialog_hold_s`, whole seconds 60–3600, default 60, PROVISIONAL bounds; chunk 2026-10-19-dialog-hold-for-the-driver); at the hold's end the wrapper replies `null` and appends one `dialog-expired` line, the dialog renders for the human in the `claude` TUI, and a later `answer` for it is refused `not-delivered` / `unknown-dialog` (exit 13) — the hold bounds the driver, never the human: any human key still hands the held dialog back at once, whatever the hold. A `viola send` on a verified CLI waits in the readiness gate for at most `GATE_MAX_WAIT` (8.5 s) and is then refused `not-delivered` / `input-not-ready` with nothing typed; a key pressed during the wait goes to the child and takes the wheel at once, and the waiting send is then refused `human-typing`. Once typed, a confirmed `viola send` waits for its confirmation within `CONFIRM_WINDOW_FALLBACK` (10 s), and a `/compact` send on a verified CLI within its own `COMPACT_CONFIRM_WINDOW` (40 s, PROVISIONAL, architecture [Delivery Confirmation]); a send not confirmed inside its window is `not-delivered` / `no-prompt-submitted`: a bound on the driver only, the confirm wait takes no key and blocks, refuses or delays none, and the wheel is untouched.

beside the options the mode word `agents`, a first word `agents` answering `agents --json` from files beside its exe (`agents-mode`, `agents-rows.json` and the live `sessions/<pid>.json` registry), built on the recorded `Agents.recorded-1.json`, with no option and no env added), the launch SessionStart is the set's recorded `SessionStart.resume-1.json` when the set holds it (2.1.287 and 2.1.302, recorded by Run E since chunk 2026-10-14-resume-and-compact-ledger-rows), else its recorded default (a set without the variant, 2.1.288), with `source` `resume` and that `session_id`, or with `--fork-session` the compiled fork id; the `--resume` shape is the `resume-session` ledger row) ; the committed Hyprland fixtures (recorded only by the test-only `viola-hypr-tap`, under the same scrub) are walked for hygiene and against their schema too, each Hyprland reply held to its closed per-request string keep-list — no insta snapshot

- Every test owns a fresh home: a not-yet-existing `home` inside `tempdir_in("<workspace>/target/e2e-home")`, so viola creates it; a test that makes a home itself makes it through `viola_state::fs::create_private_dir`, never `create_dir_all`, whose home the product refuses by the read rule, and CI's G2/G4/secret scan cover it. A test placing an endpoint in a directory of its own makes that directory through `viola_state::fs::create_private_dir` too: a bare `tempfile::tempdir()` takes its mode from the umask (`tempfile` 3.27, 0755 on a default umask), and the socket-directory check refuses it. This holds by path: on the Linux dev host `target/e2e-home` is an operator-set link to an owner-only tmpfs directory, prepared and checked by `tests/support/home.rs` `prepare_home_base` (a linked base whose filesystem reads less than `HEADROOM_FLOOR_MIB`, 9 GiB, free by `statvfs` is refused with a fixed message holding the two counts and no path; a plain base reads no headroom); no CI runner has the link. A case that needs a home viola created starts from `stamped_home`, a copy (never a link) of its build's one `viola verify` stamp, taken per pair of built binaries, kept under `target/e2e-home` keyed by the binaries' hashes and taken under an exclusive lock. Trust-start test folders sit under `/tmp`, outside any repository (a folder inside the workspace keys at its git root), an exception to test homes under `target/e2e-home`. The one home carve-out (the founder's ruling, 2026-10-04): `tests/chaos_feed_panic.rs` alone boots in `TestHome::outside_scan()` (a `viola-chaos-*` home under the system temp dir), outside G2, G4 and the secret scan, because its forced vt100 panic writes a G2-counted line; the test asserts that panic line and its `parse-rejected` line present itself.

- A census over the test sources (`every_test_verify_runs_under_a_test_home`) holds every test-started `viola verify` start tied to a test-owned home, with a closed exempt list whose every entry carries its reason, proven red on a planted untied start. A home a test gives to `viola verify --record` comes from the shared record-home helper and fixture, and no component of its path is named `home`. Every test-started `viola verify`, `viola run` and `viola revive` and every harness boot stamping runs under a test-owned user home whose config file is seeded empty and owner-only, never the runner's real `HOME` (the harness's supervised wrappers of a stamped session too, under a session user home seeded with an empty config), and the fake agent is told that config file (`--trust-config`); a `--record` verify, whose scrub reads `HOME`, keeps the real `HOME` and points a kept `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` at the test-owned user home instead. Never hand-write `ledger/stamps.json` (only `viola verify` against the fake agent), `snapshot.json` (only the wrapper, save the server-identity impostor cases' test-built snapshot, recording a held live process's pid beside the endpoint the test binds, and the MCP handler suite's own snapshots, `crates/viola-mcp/tests/handlers.rs`, whose `record_live` records an endpoint no one ever bound for the unserved row). The ban binds every booted-wrapper test; a reader's own unit cases may plant a malformed state file only by altering the writer's own bytes (write through the writer, then pad, replace or re-version).

- Steps in order: `cargo build --workspace --features viola/fake-agent` with `CARGO_TARGET_DIR=target/harness` (the CLI's `<bin dir>` is `target/harness/debug`) → a not-yet-existing home under `target/e2e-home/viola-session-*/home` (the base first prepared by `Workspace::ensure_e2e_home`: a plain directory is created; a link, as on the Linux dev host, must point at an absolute, real, owner-only directory, made again 0700 when it is gone, and refused when its filesystem reads less than the 9 GiB headroom floor free (`statvfs`), else `build-failed`) → copy the fake agent to `target/agent-run/<session>/bin/claude` on a harness-scoped `PATH` (per child via `Command::env`) → `viola verify --home` under a test-owned user home (its config file seeded empty and owner-only, the fake agent told that config file by `--trust-config`) against it with `--screens --turn-stop --trusted-root <workspace root> --dialogs --framing`, the fake agent given `--transcript` beside `--framing` (without it Run B's echo probe is skipped and the `local-command-echo` row fails) (print probe + all six interactive runs, Run B with its five added pastes (the long, tag-like and newline texts, then `/compact`, then `/clear`), its one `claude agents --json` read and, on Unix, its one probe `--settings`, and Run E, the `--resume` start of Run B's first session; every relied row, `LedgerRow::relied()`: all twenty-three) unless `--unstamped` → the `--agents-mode recorded|oversize|malformed` value (default `recorded`; a stale file removed before verify) written to the `agents-mode` file beside `bin/claude`, after verify because Run B reads `claude agents --json` through that copy, and recorded as `agents_mode` in `session.json` and `supervise.json` → `viola-harness supervise` as an ordinary child (outlives `boot`; the agent-run CLI's boot leaves it untied, stopping only via `stop.request`; it hands the fake agent `--screens --trusted-root <cwd>`; the supervised wrappers of a stamped session run under a session user home seeded with an empty config) owning one portable-pty outer PTY per instance via `viola-pty` (master writer kept until the child exits, one drain thread per master).

- Modes built: `--suppress-prompt-submit`, `--local-command-mode`, `--inject-harness-turn`, `--exit-no-eof` (its re-exec mode `--hold-stdout-internal`, which sleeps 10 s and writes nothing, is also spawned directly by the server-identity impostor cases, `tests/security_negatives_server_identity.rs` and `tests/hook_fail_open.rs`, as the live process their snapshot records, reaped by each file's `Held` `Drop` guard), `--report-version`, `--trim-prompt-end` (a bracketed paste plus Enter fires UserPromptSubmit with its trailing run of space, TAB, CR and LF removed), `--framing` (verify's Run B: a compiled paste text fires its recorded `paste-<n>` variant unchanged, the probed `/clear` its recorded `clear-<n>` SessionEnd then SessionStart and no UserPromptSubmit, and the probed `/compact` the recorded `SessionStart.compact-1` with the last fired SessionStart's `session_id` and no UserPromptSubmit), the capped test-only hold `--paste-hint-ms` (10 s at most: a cleared screen after the long paste's turn), the test-only screen switch `--tag-turn-screen <phase>` (with `--framing` and `--turn-stop`: `Screen.<phase>` of the set after the tag-like paste's turn alone, in place of `Screen.turn`), the test-only screen switch `--long-turn-screen <phase>` (with `--framing` and `--turn-stop`: `Screen.<phase>` of the set after the long paste's turn alone, after its Stop, in place of `Screen.turn`), `--vt100-panic-bytes` (after its `start` receipt it writes `e4 b8 ad` once to its terminal; under a 24×1 PTY that panics vt100's feed). `--transcript` (argv-only) creates `<exe dir>/transcripts/` at 0700 at start and gives the launch SessionStart a `transcript_path` to a seeded 0600 file named by its session id (replayed framing variants not rewritten); under `--local-command-mode` a submitted local command whose post-condition is the stdout tag, and under `--framing` the exact verify echo probe command, append one stdout tag line to the last started session's transcript and fire no hook. `--settings <file>` is accepted, its value consumed and ignored. `--trust-config <file>` reads trust from that config file by the CLI's walk (the canonical cwd's exact key, then each parent up to the git root, so inside a repository the cwd's own record counts) through a bounded read; any failure reads untrusted. Under `--screens` with an untrusted cwd it draws claude 2.1.325's unnumbered trust form over the set's recorded modal (selector first on No, directly above the recorded trust row, row 16 with no recorded modal); arrows move the selector, Enter on No exits 1, and the launch SessionStart fires only after Enter on the trust row, which draws the ready screen. Built for `viola revive`'s tests and, under the fake agent, verify's Run E: `--resume <id>` (the launch SessionStart reports source `resume` and that id) and `--fork-session` (beside `--resume`, the compiled fork id; alone it changes nothing); and the capped test-only hold `--stop-receipt-hold-ms` (1 000 ms at most, holding the Stop hook's receipt to force a race window open), and the test-only hold `--trust-record-blank` (a start trusted by the trust record alone draws no screen, holding verify's Run F window open for a stop case). Built: the mode word `agents` (a first word `agents` answers `agents --json` from files beside its exe: `agents-mode` (`recorded` · `oversize` · `malformed`, absent = `recorded`), `agents-rows.json` (planted rows) and the live `sessions/<pid>.json` registry, a row written just before its launch SessionStart fires, a dead or reused pid skipped through one `viola_state::liveness::start_times()` read; built on the recorded `Agents.recorded-1.json`; no option and no env added). Exits on `\x03` or at stdin EOF, and exits 1 on Enter on the trust form's No, first waiting for a hook still running and starting no other; on Unix every command it spawns (each hook) runs in a process group of its own (`process_group(0)`, as the `--exit-no-eof` holder does), because a hangup of its PTY's foreground group, at its exit as session leader or when a killed wrapper closes the PTY, cuts a `viola hook` short in its exit-time coverage write (a cut-short profile, measured); the agent itself, its PTY's session leader, cannot leave that group (`setpgid` refuses a leader), so on Unix its exit ignores SIGHUP from its first step (`\x03` or stdin's end): a hangup that lands while it exits (a killed wrapper, or portable-pty's SIGHUP-first kill) no longer cuts its own exit-time coverage write, and one that lands before the exit begins still ends it (measured). That exit, shared Unix code, is witnessed on Linux only: `tests/cli_fake_agent.rs` `fake_agent_exit_outlives_a_hangup_that_lands_while_it_exits` (`cfg(target_os = "linux")`) reads the SIGHUP disposition through `ps -o sigignore= -p <pid>`; it runs on CI's one leg, `ubuntu-latest`.

- Root fixture chain: `tests/support/` (`home` → `fake_agent_path` → `stamped_home`, a copy, never a link, of one `viola verify` stamp per build (taken against the fake agent at 2.1.287 over `fixtures/claude` under a test-owned user home whose config file is seeded empty and owner-only, the fake agent told that config file (a `--record` verify keeps the real HOME and points a kept `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` at the test-owned user home instead), the fake agent given `--transcript` beside `--framing`, once per pair of built binaries, under an exclusive lock, kept under `target/e2e-home` keyed by the binaries' hashes) → `booted_wrapper`; `StampedHome::unstamped` for the unverified path; every long-lived viola child a root test spawns is tied to its spawning test thread by a parent-death kill (spawned only on a thread that outlives it; exiting when its recorded parent is already gone; `cross_killed_test_census_finds_no_untied_viola_spawn` finds no untied viola spawn in any test source; `every_test_verify_runs_under_a_test_home` holds every test-started `viola verify` start tied to a test-owned home, and every test-started `viola run` and `viola revive` runs under a test-owned user home, never the runner's real HOME, with a closed exempt list whose every entry carries its reason, proven red on a planted untied start), so a killed or panicked test leaves no wrapper or fake agent, and a Drop guard that kills, then waits, still covers the normal end; `Wrapper::stop` waits for the endpoint to be unconnectable, not only the exit; `wait_ready` at its deadline appends the stalled wrapper's state — its last `run-<name>.ndjson` event, its `/proc/<pid>/wchan` and the `stat` state field (`note_stall`) — to the watch report before the panic, signalling nothing and adding nothing to a passing boot). Homes live under `target/e2e-home/viola-test-*` (the base prepared by `prepare_home_base` under the harness keeper's contract; on the Linux dev host it is a link to an owner-only tmpfs directory, so removals reach outside the working directory and a kept home does not survive a reboot), kept per `AGENT_RUN_KEEP_HOMES` / `AGENT_RUN_KEEP_FAILED` (viola-e2e's booted lifecycle tests: a `Booted` drop guard stops the session, then keeps the home only for a panicking test under `AGENT_RUN_KEEP_FAILED=1`); each records `owner.json` `{pid, started_at}`, and a new home (no keep flag set) first removes only dirs whose recorded owner process is gone — never by age or name, never a dir without a record, save a build's verify stamp dir, which carries none: another build's stamp is swept only when its lock is taken without waiting (a runner-killed test never drops its home); the drop and that sweep both go through `remove_owned`, which deletes `owner.json` last, so a removal that stops part-way keeps the record. The chain exists once, as the sync root copy in `tests/support/`: viola-e2e has no copy and boots its sessions through its own `harness_session`; Path 1's flow lands on the root chain as `tests/path1_run_start.rs`.

- The hidden capture arm, `hook <event> --capture`, does no obs init and writes no line (a bounded panic-line exemption, obs-plan §10). `viola verify` runs `strict::check_home_tree` on the home, `ledger/`, `bin/` and `plugin/` before its `cli` log opens: a refused tree is exit 1 with the home pair, no step line, no log and no line; a refused `update_stamps` (`StampsError::StrictModes`, nothing read or written) prints the same pair and exits 1 through its own `process-exit`, which under a parsed `VIOLA_NAME` carries `detail:"strict-modes-failed"`; every other refusal past the tree check writes its own code there (`program-not-found`, `pinned-hash-mismatch`, `version-unreadable`, `unclean-fixture`), a failing row is no refusal and carries no code, and the fixture's `<file>` enters no code. `viola verify`'s trust-record write and removal emit no log line and no span (a refused symlinked, non-regular or foreign file included); the outcome rides only the stamps. Each wrapped start of `viola run` and `viola revive` on a verified CLI opens no span for its trust step and writes exactly one INFO `trust-record` line to the run role file, its required `detail` one of a closed set of 16 start words (`trust-record` in the event enum of both the diag-line and the detail-line schema), and the word never refuses the start; no path, key or value of the claude config reaches any line, stamp or summary. A `viola verify` stopped by Ctrl-C or TERM (`SIGINT` / `SIGTERM`) starts no further spawn, kills and reaps the child it is running, closes every spawn pair it opened (a child of an interactive PTY run killed at the stop closes with `duration_ms` and a `child_exit_status`, the PTY pump's exit code; a print-mode or `--version` probe child killed at the stop is not measured) and ends `process-exit{subject:"self", exit_code:1, detail:"interrupted"}` (a member of the `process-exit` `detail` enum `schemas/diag-line.v1.json` closes at 19 values); `run`'s version gate observes no stop.
